lessons.title: One account across past, present, and future
lessons.explanation: This lesson assembles everything in the level: roles marked by case, actions presented by aspect, and time located by tense. Take one realistic account and read it in three slots. Вчера я весь день писала отчёт (vchee-RA ya vyes' dyen pee-SA-la at-CHYOT) — Yesterday I wrote the report all day: past tense, imperfective verb, and a duration phrase of the kind that favours the imperfective because the sentence measures how the day was spent rather than asserting completion. Сейчас я читаю статью (see-CHAS ya chee-TA-yu sta-TYOO) — Right now I am reading an article: present tense, which in Russian exists only for imperfective verbs, with the accusative object статья in its -ю form. Завтра я напишу отчёт и отправлю его (ZAF-tra ya na-pee-SHOO at-CHYOT ee at-PRAV-lyu ee-VO) — Tomorrow I will finish the report and send it: two perfective non-past forms, which mean future, and no auxiliary verb at all. Add a bounded interval and the compound future appears instead: Через час я буду читать (CHYE-ryes chas ya BOO-du chee-TAT) — In an hour I will be reading, where буду carries the future and the imperfective infinitive carries the activity. Three time slots, three different arrangements of the same small system.
lessons.example: Now revise a single fact and watch how far the change travels. Suppose tomorrow will not finish the report, because only an hour is free and no result is promised. Revise the last sentence to Завтра я буду писать отчёт (ZAF-tra ya BOO-du pee-SAT at-CHYOT) — Tomorrow I will be writing the report and leave the two earlier sentences untouched: yesterday's duration phrase and today's reading have not changed. The past sentences are not dragged along by the future revision, which is a discipline worth practising, because learners often rewrite an entire account when a single commitment changes. Now change a different kind of fact. Suppose the report has already been sent, so the account is entirely past: Вчера я весь день писала отчёт, а вечером я написала его и отправила (vchee-RA ya vyes' dyen pee-SA-la at-CHYOT a VYE-chee-ram ya na-pee-SA-la ee-VO ee at-PRA-vee-la) — Yesterday I wrote the report all day, and in the evening I finished it and sent it. The contrast between the day-long imperfective and the two evening perfectives is the background-and-foreground pattern from lesson 59, now inside one sentence pair.
lessons.question: Why does Завтра я напишу отчёт use no future auxiliary, while Через час я буду читать does?
lessons.answer: Because написать is perfective, so its non-past form already means future, while читать is imperfective and needs the auxiliary буду plus its infinitive to place the activity in the future.
lessons.distractor: Because writing a report is a completed action while reading is not, and only completed actions may use the auxiliary.
lessons.correction: The auxiliary is not reserved for incomplete actions; it is reserved for imperfective verbs. The compound future буду plus infinitive is the future construction of the imperfective, and the perfective builds its own future from the non-past endings. Both sentences describe future activity involving a report or an article; the difference is which aspect each verb belongs to. A useful check is to look for the auxiliary: if буду is present, the infinitive after it must be imperfective.

depth.definitions: A time slot in this lesson is a rough division of the timeline into past, present, and future. Aspect is the presentation of an action as a process or a bounded whole; tense locates the action in time. A compound future is the auxiliary буду with an imperfective infinitive; a simple future is a perfective verb in a non-past form. Cohesion is what holds a text together, including repeated participants, consistent time reference, and sequencing markers. Cornell's tense page presents the whole grid in one table, with past on both aspects, present only on the imperfective, and two distinct future constructions.[20]
depth.mechanism: Three decisions generate every sentence in the account, and keeping them separate is the point of this lesson. First, choose the participant roles and mark them by case: subject in the dictionary form, object in the accusative, a setting in the prepositional, an origin or beneficiary in the genitive. Second, choose the presentation: process or bounded whole. Third, choose the time slot and with it the construction that slot permits, which for the future means either буду plus an imperfective infinitive or a perfective non-past form.[20][21] Because the three decisions are independent, an error in one does not excuse an error in another, and a sentence can be right in time and wrong in aspect. Two limits belong here. First, aspect is not a register marker: using the perfective is not more confident or more polite than using the imperfective, it simply asserts a bounded event, and using it to sound decisive changes what the sentence claims. Second, no grammatical choice can guarantee that events occur, so a perfective future is a projection or an intention rather than evidence of success.
depth.secondExample: Rebuild the account from the perspective of a reader rather than a writer. Сейчас я читаю статью (see-CHAS ya chee-TA-yu sta-TYOO) — Right now I am reading an article is present and imperfective. Пока я читала, Анна написала отчёт (pa-KA ya chee-TA-la AN-na na-pee-SA-la at-CHYOT) — While I was reading, Anna finished the report sets a background activity beside one completed event, which is the two-level organisation of lesson 59 in a different pair of participants. Завтра я прочитаю статью и напишу отзыв (ZAF-tra ya pra-chee-TA-yu sta-TYOO ee na-pee-SHOO AT-zyf) — Tomorrow I will read the article through and write a review: two perfective futures in sequence, each presenting one bounded act. Now exchange one verb for a process and notice that the whole sentence changes its claim: Завтра я буду читать статью и писать отзыв (ZAF-tra ya BOO-du chee-TAT sta-TYOO ee pee-SAT AT-zyf) — Tomorrow I will be reading the article and writing a review promises time spent rather than results delivered. The participants are identical, the case forms are identical, and only the aspect of the verbs tells your listener what you are committing to.
depth.mistake: Four errors appear at this stage, and each has a different repair. The first is an aspect error, such as using a perfective verb with a duration phrase, which needs the time phrase and the presentation brought back into agreement. The second is a tense-construction error, such as буду писать from a perfective form or an auxiliary added to a perfective infinitive, which needs the two future patterns kept apart. The third is a case error inside a correctly chosen verb, which needs the role labelling you practised in the first unit. The fourth is a discourse error: a grammatically correct account with no sequencing markers and no consistent time reference, which needs markers and a stable anchor rather than more grammar. Diagnose by category and practise the category that failed; repeating the whole account faster will not repair a specific gap.
depth.application: This closes the level, so the task is a written project with a rubric rather than a drill. Write a six-sentence account of your real week with at least two sentences in the past, two in the present or immediate present, and two in the future; include at least one animate object, one location, one destination, one origin or beneficiary, one duration phrase, and one sequencing marker. Model account: Вчера я весь день писала отчёт (vchee-RA ya vyes' dyen pee-SA-la at-CHYOT) — Yesterday I wrote the report all day; Потом я читала статью о работе (pa-TOM ya chee-TA-la sta-TYOO a ra-BO-tye) — Then I read an article about work; Сейчас я живу около работы (see-CHAS ya zhee-VOO O-ka-la ra-BO-ty) — Right now I live near work; Каждый день я читаю по-русски (KAZH-dy dyen ya chee-TA-yu pa-ROO-skee) — Every day I read in Russian; Завтра я напишу отчёт и отправлю его (ZAF-tra ya na-pee-SHOO at-CHYOT ee at-PRAV-lyu ee-VO) — Tomorrow I will finish the report and send it; Через час я буду читать книгу для Анны (CHYE-ryes chas ya BOO-du chee-TAT KNEE-goo dlya AN-ny) — In an hour I will be reading a book for Anna. Self-review rubric with five criteria: (1) every case ending matches a role you can name; (2) every time phrase agrees with its verb's aspect; (3) present-tense sentences use only imperfective verbs; (4) every future sentence uses one of the two permitted constructions; (5) the account includes at least one sequencing marker so the listener can follow it. Mark each criterion secure, developing, or needs review, cite one sentence as evidence for each, and rewrite only the sentences that failed. No result on this task certifies general fluency; it reports the state of these specific skills.
depth.summary: Three independent decisions produce a Russian sentence: roles marked by case, presentation marked by aspect, and time marked by tense and construction. Keeping them separate is what allows you to revise one without damaging the others. The level assessment that follows samples these decisions in new combinations; reading it through is not evidence of the skills, and producing the account unaided is the better evidence.

visual.title: Three time slots, one system
visual.description: A labelled sequence for building an account that moves from the past through the present to the future.
steps: Anchor each sentence in one time slot and mark it with a time expression or a sequencing word.
For past sentences, choose the aspect that matches the job: process or scene for the imperfective, advancing event for the perfective.
For present sentences, use an imperfective verb only, and signal habit or current activity with an adverb such as каждый день or сейчас.
For future sentences, choose either буду with an imperfective infinitive to present activity, or a perfective non-past form to present a bounded event.
Assign case roles inside each sentence and check the endings, then read the account aloud and confirm the time reference never contradicts itself.

questions.prompt: You meet сказать in a text and need its imperfective partner for a sentence about speaking in general. How do you proceed?
questions.answer: Use говорить, a partner with a different root, and confirm partners in a dictionary rather than deriving them.
questions.distractor: Add the suffix -ыва- to сказать to build сказивать, since imperfectives are derived from perfectives by suffixation.
questions.correction: The -ыва- and -ива- suffixes do produce imperfective partners for many verbs, but they do not apply to every verb, and сказать is paired with говорить, which shares no root. Cornell states that there is no sure way to derive a verb's aspect partner, which is why the reliable route is a dictionary entry or a teaching list rather than a morphological guess.

questions.prompt: A learner writes Я сделаю отчёт сейчас to mean I am getting the report done right now. What does the sentence actually mean, and what form is needed?
questions.answer: The perfective non-past form refers to the future, so the sentence means I will do the report; for the present, use the imperfective Я делаю отчёт.
questions.distractor: The sentence is present in meaning, but it needs the auxiliary буду to make the aspect match.
questions.correction: The form is not defective and no auxiliary will repair it. Сделать is perfective, and a perfective non-past form has future reference, so the sentence projects a bounded event. An action happening now requires an imperfective verb, which is why the present tense in Russian exists only for imperfective forms.

questions.prompt: A learner writes Я делал это за два часа to mean it took me two hours to finish. What is the diagnosis and the repair?
questions.answer: За plus a duration presupposes completion, so the verb should be perfective: Я сделал это за два часа.
questions.distractor: The sentence is correct as written, because за expresses duration in the same way as a bare accusative.
questions.correction: The two phrases ask different questions. A bare accusative duration reports how long an activity lasted, which fits the imperfective, while за plus a duration reports how long completion took, which presupposes a bounded whole. Pairing за with the imperfective leaves the sentence asserting a duration for an activity whose endpoint was never claimed.

questions.prompt: A learner drafts Я прочитал, когда позвонила Анна. Why does the sentence fail as narration, and what is the repair?
questions.answer: The reading is the ongoing background and needs the imperfective: Я читал, когда позвонила Анна.
questions.distractor: The call is too brief for the perfective, so both verbs should be imperfective.
questions.correction: Briefness is not the issue; the call is a single completed event and belongs in the perfective, which carries the account forward. The problem is the first verb, which has been turned into a completed act and therefore no longer supplies a scene for the call to interrupt. In this pattern the imperfective holds the background and the perfective supplies the event.

questions.prompt: You must report that yesterday was spent writing the report and that tomorrow will finish it. Which forms fit, and why?
questions.answer: Use the imperfective past with the duration phrase for yesterday, and a perfective non-past form for tomorrow's completed result.
questions.distractor: Use perfective past for yesterday's work and буду plus the perfective infinitive for tomorrow's result.
questions.correction: Yesterday's sentence measures how the day was spent, so the duration phrase favours the imperfective regardless of the outcome: Вчера я весь день писала отчёт. Tomorrow's sentence asserts a bounded result, which the perfective non-past supplies: Завтра я напишу отчёт. The distractor fails on both counts, because буду never takes a perfective infinitive.

questions.prompt: A feminine speaker reports that yesterday she saw Anna and read the book. Three endings must be chosen independently: the object Анна, the object книга, and the past verb. Analyse which word controls each ending, and explain why superficially similar endings do not share a single rule.
questions.answer: я controls the verb, so the past form is читала; both noun objects are feminine -а nouns, whose accusative ending is -у whatever their animacy, giving Анну and книгу.
questions.distractor: All three take -у because every feminine word in the sentence receives the same feminine ending.
questions.correction: Agreement and case are different systems. The subject я determines the verb's feminine singular past form, while each object's ending follows its own declension; for feminine -а nouns the accusative is -у for animate and inanimate nouns alike, and the animacy contrast shows up in the plural and in masculine singular nouns instead. Naming the controlling word for every ending prevents mistaking one repeated sound for one rule.

questions.prompt: One message says you are at the university and the next says you are walking to the university. The same preposition в appears in both. State the case each phrase requires and explain what carries the difference for your reader.
questions.answer: The location takes the prepositional and the destination takes the accusative; the noun ending, not the preposition, carries the distinction.
questions.distractor: Both phrases take the accusative, because в always marks movement toward something.
questions.correction: В is neutral about movement; its meaning shifts with the case that follows it. A goal of motion takes the accusative, and a setting takes the prepositional, so the two sentences differ in the noun's form even though the preposition is identical. A learner who considers only the preposition cannot tell the two sentences apart, which is why relationship comes before form.

questions.prompt: You report that a letter arrived from Moscow and that a parcel is intended for Anna. Choose the two prepositions and the case each requires, then explain the reasoning that keeps them from being confused with their near neighbours от and the dative.
questions.answer: Из plus the genitive Москвы marks a place source, and для plus the genitive Анны marks a beneficiary.
questions.distractor: От plus the genitive Москвы marks the source, and the dative Анне marks the beneficiary.
questions.correction: От is used when the source is a person, so it cannot be used of Moscow; из is used for places and enclosed spaces. Для marks a person for whose benefit something is intended and takes the genitive, whereas the dative Анне would mark a recipient of a transferred object, as in giving her the parcel directly. Classifying the relation first prevents both mistakes.

questions.prompt: Your supply list must deny one notebook, deny several notebooks, and deny available time. Give the three phrases and explain what changes across them, using the noun's class and the kind of thing being denied.
questions.answer: Нет тетради for one notebook, нет тетрадей for several, and нет времени for time, which stays singular as a mass noun.
questions.distractor: Нет тетради for all three, because нет always takes the genitive singular.
questions.correction: Нет requires the genitive but does not fix the number; number follows what you deny. A single item is genitive singular, a countable set is genitive plural, and a mass noun such as time remains singular. The plural shape depends on the noun's class: a soft-sign feminine noun takes -ей, giving тетрадей, while a hard masculine noun would add -ов.

questions.prompt: Analyse Вчера я купила книгу для Анны в магазине около дома. Name the case of each noun phrase and identify the word that selected it, then state which parts are agreement rather than case.
questions.answer: Я is the subject, купила agrees with it in feminine past, книгу is the verb's accusative object, для selected the genitive Анны, в selected the prepositional магазине as a setting, and около selected the genitive дома.
questions.distractor: Every noun phrase after the verb is genitive, because Russian marks all non-subject phrases with the genitive in long sentences.
questions.correction: There is no such general rule. Each phrase is governed by the word that introduces it: the verb купить selects an accusative object, для and около each select the genitive for unrelated reasons, and в selects the prepositional when the noun names a setting rather than a goal. Купила is agreement with the subject rather than a case at all, so agreement and government must be tracked separately.

questions.prompt: A learner claims that any perfective partner can be produced by prefixing the imperfective verb. Give a counterexample from this level and explain the two distinct reasons the claim fails.
questions.answer: Брать and взять share no root, so no prefix could produce the partner; and a prefix may change a verb's meaning instead of only its aspect.
questions.distractor: The claim fails only for verbs of motion, because those have two imperfective forms instead of an imperfective and a perfective.
questions.correction: Pairs are formed in several ways, including stem modification and suppletion, so prefixation is only one route. Even where a prefix is present, Cornell distinguishes three outcomes of prefixing a simple verb: the same meaning as a perfective partner, a different meaning, or a different verb entirely. Since the same device can add aspect or add meaning, partners must be recorded and checked rather than derived.

questions.prompt: Why can Я сделаю это сейчас not describe an action in progress, and what would you say instead? Explain the general principle that settles the choice without reference to this particular verb.
questions.answer: Сделать is perfective, so its non-past form refers to the future; the present requires an imperfective verb, as in Я делаю это сейчас.
questions.distractor: Сейчас cannot be used with a perfective verb, so the adverb is the reason the sentence fails.
questions.correction: The adverb is not the cause; remove it and the sentence still means I will do it. The general principle is that Russian builds the present only from imperfective non-past forms, so a perfective non-past form necessarily projects a bounded event into the future. The repair is a change of verb, not of adverb.

questions.prompt: You report both that you were reading for two hours and that you read the article in two hours. Beyond the verb form, what changes, and how would you explain the difference to someone who thinks the two time phrases measure the same interval?
questions.answer: The phrases measure different things: a bare accusative measures how long the activity lasted, while за plus the same quantity measures how long completion took.
questions.distractor: Only the tense changes; both phrases measure the same interval and merely differ in formality.
questions.correction: Each phrase carries a presupposition. A duration answering how long you spent does not assert an endpoint, which suits the imperfective. За with a duration answers how long it took to finish, which presupposes completion, which suits the perfective. The interval may be numerically identical, but what the sentence claims about the action is not.

questions.prompt: In Когда я вошёл, все читали, identify the event and the background, then explain what a reader would understand differently if both verbs were perfective.
questions.answer: Вошёл is the single event and читали is the background activity; making both perfective would present two completed incidents in sequence rather than a scene interrupted.
questions.distractor: A когда clause always supplies the background, so вошёл would have to be imperfective for the sentence to be coherent.
questions.correction: A когда clause can hold either level; the aspect of its verb decides. With an imperfective in that clause you present a scene; with a perfective you present an event that interrupts or advances the account. Two perfectives remain grammatical but change the reading from a description of a scene to a sequence of incidents.

questions.prompt: Your plan states three things: you read all day yesterday, you will be reading in an hour, and you will finish the report tomorrow. Name the three constructions and justify each choice.
questions.answer: An imperfective past with the duration phrase, then буду plus an imperfective infinitive, then a perfective non-past form for tomorrow's result.
questions.distractor: A perfective past for yesterday, a perfective future for the reading, and буду plus a perfective infinitive for tomorrow.
questions.correction: Yesterday's sentence measures how the day was spent, so the imperfective is needed whichever verb you choose. The hour from now is an interval of activity, which the compound future presents with an imperfective infinitive. Tomorrow's sentence asserts a bounded result, which the perfective non-past supplies without an auxiliary. The distractor fails because буду never combines with a perfective infinitive.

questions.prompt: A future commitment loses its endpoint, so tomorrow becomes reading time rather than a finished report. State exactly what must change in the account and what must stay as it is, with reasons.
questions.answer: The future construction changes from a perfective non-past form to буду plus an imperfective infinitive; the object's case and any earlier past sentences stay unchanged.
questions.distractor: Every sentence in the account becomes imperfective, including the past sentences, so that the whole account presents activity rather than results.
questions.correction: Revise the commitment that changed, not the facts that did not. The object remains accusative because the participant roles are untouched, and yesterday's sentences are unaffected by tomorrow's intention. Altering unrelated sentences damages information your listener may already be relying on, and it also obscures which decision you were actually revising.

questions.prompt: A learner has read this level and recognises every model but cannot produce an unaided account. What should the feedback distinguish, and what single next action should it prescribe?
questions.answer: Distinguish recognition from independent production, and prescribe retrieval practice on the specific category that failed rather than more reading.
questions.distractor: Recognition of the models is sufficient evidence, so the level can be marked complete without further production practice.
questions.correction: Recognising a model and producing it under time pressure are different skills supported by different evidence. The feedback should name the failing category, for example case roles, aspect with time phrases, or the future constructions, and prescribe targeted retrieval and a rewritten account. Completing the readings is a record of reading position, not a claim about competence.
